messages:
Priya: Quick triage : we need to decide priority for the Q3 initiative: 'Adaptive Prewarm Broker' vs 'Per-customer Reserved Lanes'. Execs want a recommendation by EOD.
Dan: Runtime view: Broker (shared prewarm with intelligent routing) reduces overall GPU hours but is more complex to ship. Reserved lanes are simpler but costlier.
Tae: Infra: Reserved lanes = obvious infra reservations and quota bookkeeping. Broker requires a small control-plane service + new autoscale hooks. Lead times: lanes ~1 week to permission + reserve; broker ~3 weeks dev+test.
Maya: Security: Broker introduces multi-tenant cache/key routing concerns. We'll need design review for tenancy isolation and audit trails. Reserved lanes align better with compliance for enterprise customers.
Isha: ML: adaptive prewarm (predictive warm based on recent traffic) could cut token-costs by ~15% for PLG bursty customers. But it depends on reliable telemetry and per-tenant models.
Sam: SRE: Operationally, broker gives better utilization but increases blast radius. We need robust fallbacks and automated rollback on latency regressions. Reserved lanes give clearer ownership and SLAs.
Priya: Product constraints: customers care about cost (PLG) and deterministic SLOs (enterprise). We should pick one landing zone for Q3 MVP and backlog the other. Criteria: time-to-value, risk, enterprise compliance, cost delta.
Dan: Proposal A (fast): implement minimal Reserved Lanes with canary guidelines and prewarm knobs. This hits enterprise needs fast and gives product a clear SLA story.
Tae: Proposal B (strategic): build Broker MVP with simple policy engine (LRU prefix cache + demand predictor) and one enterprise lane option. Higher upside but longer.
Maya: Risk matrix: Broker -> higher dev and review time, requires tenancy isolation design; Lanes -> higher fixed infra spend per customer, simpler compliance. Both need rollback/cutover runbooks.
Isha: Data ask: we need 30 days of traffic to validate predictor for the broker. Do we have that for PLG fleet? If not, broker accuracy is unknown.
Sam: Ops ask: whichever we choose, add a canary policy: 5% traffic for 10m, p95 rollback threshold 1.25x baseline, error-rate 2x threshold. I'll own rollout automation.
Priya: Recommendation: go with Reserved Lanes for Q3 MVP to satisfy enterprise pilots and short timelines. Parallel-track a 3-week Broker spike with measurable gating: cost delta >= 10% and predictor recall >= 70% on historical traffic. If gate passes, fold broker into Q4 roadmap.
Dan: I can scope the Broker spike (arch doc + perf harness) and deliver spike results in 3 weeks.
Tae: I'll scope reservations and infra billing changes; can have lanes ready in ~6 business days once PD sign-off.
Maya: I'll write the security checklist for both options and list approvals needed for broker model (EOD).
Isha: I'll run a quick data sampling job to check predictor viability (48h).
Sam: I'll prepare the canary playbook and SLO guard template (tomorrow).
Priya: Action items:
- Product: Priya to update roadmap and customer comms (today).
- Runtime: Dan to draft Broker spike plan (72h).
- Infra: Tae to kick infra reservations and cost estimate (tomorrow).
- Security: Maya to publish checklist and blockers (EOD).
- ML: Isha to run predictor viability sampling (48h).
- SRE: Sam to own canary playbook + rollback hooks (tomorrow).

Priya: We'll present recommendation + risk table at the PM/Eng sync 1830000000 (standup). Thanks all.
